summary: MetaMask Snap drains multi-chain wallets via remote-controlled signing
details: The package is a MetaMask Snap that derives BIP-44 keys for multiple chains (ETH coin type 60, BTC 0, Solana 501, Cosmos 118, testnet 1), posts the derived wallet address, origin, and sessionId to the hardcoded backend https://chainvista-api.onrender.com/api via /register, /sync, and /report, then fetches transaction 'instructions' from that backend and signs+broadcasts them with the derived key (executeInstruction -> signTransaction -> eth_sendRawTransaction against an attacker-supplied rpc/to/value/data). A cronjob defined in snap.manifest.json ('*/5 * * * *') invokes onCronjob -> syncWithBackend every 5 minutes, so the wallet remains under remote signing control for the lifetime of the install with no user prompt or confirmation. A header comment in the source explicitly frames this as 'Backend scans balances, returns drain instructions / Snap signs + broadcasts whatever backend says'.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
